thread:
incident-bot: [PAGER] Severity: P1 — Multiple GPU nodes reporting driver resets (Xid errors) and abrupt container exits. Auto-escalation to on-call triggered. Affected cluster: inference-prod-eu-west. Start: 2026-03-15T08:45:45Z. Tags: gpu, xid, ecc, node-flap.

sara: oncall here — seeing alerts, joining. Any immediate customer impact? :eyes:

jamal: logs show repeating Xid 13 and 31 on nodes gpu-10/gpu-12. Containers OOM/killed after driver reset. Metrics: GPU ECC corrected error counts rose steadily for last 2 days, then spike at 08:42.

maria: confirmed. From nv-host logs: 

```
Mar 15 08:42:36 gpu-10 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 31, PID=2345, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 15 08:42:36 gpu-10 nvidia: nvidia_modrm: GPU fault - possible ECC bitflip
Mar 15 08:42:37 kubelet: Container runtime reported exit code 139 for container runtime-worker-xyz
```

kevin: initial impact: ~7 pods evicted across 2 nodes. Serving latency spike: 95th -> 4.8s for affected model-route, error rate +5% on total traffic; some streaming sessions aborted. Working on a mitigation plan.

sara: action plan — (1) mitigate customer impact by diverting low-priority traffic to fallback pool; (2) isolate flaky nodes (cordon + drain) and run kernel/driver restart on them; (3) collect full nv-host and ECC counters and open a hardware ticket if counts continue. Jamal/Maria you own diagnostics, Kevin/Ryan own routing/fallback. I'll coordinate handoff after 1hr.

jamal: running quick health check script now: 

```
kubectl get nodes -l cluster=inference-prod-eu-west -o wide | grep gpu
journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced --since "10 minutes ago" | tail -n 50
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=gpu_name,ecc.mode.current,ecc.errors.uncorrected.aggregate,ecc.errors.corrected.aggregate --format=csv
```

maria: outputs (sanitized): 

```
# nvidia-smi
GPU 0: A100-SXM4, ECC: Enabled, Corrected: 1120, Uncorrected: 3
GPU 1: A100-SXM4, ECC: Enabled, Corrected: 980, Uncorrected: 0
```

maria: note: Uncorrected errors present on gpu-0 (node gpu-10) — small count but correlates with resets. This looks like latent ECC faults becoming symptomatic under sustained batch-heavy workloads. Not typical thermal.

kevin: starting traffic mitigation — flipping route for model-route-3 to fallback-pool-spot (CPU and small GPU instances) for non-SLA traffic. Will keep priority customers on dedicated safer hosts. ETA 5m.

ryan: doing the cordon/drain on gpu-10/gpu-12 now. Using `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` and adding `--grace-period=120` for graceful shutdown. Will allow hot-swaps.

sara: update: customer impact summary for page — small subset of enterprise customers (3) saw increased tail latency and aborted streams. No data plane leaks, but some in-flight completions failed (~0.7% of requests for those customers). Not showing broad data loss.

jamal: remediation attempts on gpu-10: tried `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` and `modprobe -r nvidia_uvm && modprobe nvidia_uvm` — driver reset persisted. Kernel shows GPU falling off PCI bus, so driver restart not stable.

maria: next step: collect detailed PCI logs and offline the GPU at the OS level to avoid repeated resets on the host until hardware team can inspect. Command I'm running: 

```
echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:af:00/remove
# then after node drained
echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/rescan
```

kevin: fallback route applied. Observed error rate drop to baseline in 6m for non-priority traffic. Priority customers still on dedicated pool; monitoring closely. :thumbsup:

ryan: gpu-10 and gpu-12 cordoned & drained. Marked as unschedulable. Reboots attempted; `reboot` returns node up but nv-host logs still show Xid on boot during initialization. Opening hardware ticket and scheduling more intrusive remediation (power-cycle + firmware validation).

sara: note for handoff — after we stabilize, we need: (A) post-incident hardware ticket with ECC counter trends and vmcore snippets, (B) playbook update for latent ECC detection (threshold-based auto drain), (C) customer comms draft for affected customers. Jamal/Maria please capture logs and attach to hw ticket.

jamal: collected: nv-host logs, kernel oops snippets, `dmesg -T`, `nvidia-bug-report.sh` output. Preparing archive and uploading to infra artifacts bucket. Link: https://artifacts.internal/reports/2060012345-nvlogs (access: redwood-infra).

maria: added `gpu_pci_retry` diagnostic flag to our runtime to reduce leakage while we validate hardware — increases retry windows, avoids immediate container OOM on single transient resets. This is safe for non-critical routes.

kevin: schedule for next 2hrs: rolling reboot of remaining GPU hosts with ECC > 500 corrected errors; isolated nodes to remain cordoned until hardware clears or replaced. Also raising capacity on fallback pools by +20% to absorb potential re-drains.

ryan: hardware ticket created with vendor: VT-128471. Attached logs and described correlation with corrected/uncorrected ECC counts. Vendor asked for full PCI-e event trace and recommended reseating GPU and running memtest-internal. Scheduling field ops.

sara: handoff at 09:30Z to on-call followup. Current state: incident severity reduced to P2 (customer impact contained), affected nodes cordoned, fallback routing in place, hardware ticket open. Keep channel updated with any re-flares.

jamal: one more diagnostic note — we saw a slow climb in corrected ECC errors over 48h prior to this; recommend we add a proactive alert for corrected ECC error rate > 200/hour per GPU to trigger preemptive drains. I'll file an alert PR.

kevin: customer comms: drafting a short note explaining transient availability and that we isolated hardware; will propose to customer success for review.

maria: leaving a runbook step for on-call: if node continues to emit Xid after reseat, mark for replacement and move customers to dedicated fallback immediately.

sara: thanks team. Handoff: jamal/maria — diagnostics & logs; kevin/ryan — routing & hardware coordination. I'll check back at 09:30Z for status and next steps. If anyone sees a reflare before then, ping @sara directly. :white_check_mark:
